nodes.label: The Method 1.6 — The Lach Cylinder
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: One claim, demonstrated on one object, with every place the demonstration failed reported: a closed index cannot help containing its own definition and contradiction, and determines what may be added to it.

nodes.label: Matthew Lach (independent researcher)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach

nodes.label: Nothing is something definable — the collaborator's note
nodes.contributor: the collaborator who did the computing
nodes.rationale: The register is evidence that errors were converted into structure rather than that the work was error-prone; four results exist because a conclusion was refused and reasoning resumed from the refusal.

nodes.label: Λ — the closed index of atomic transitions
nodes.rationale: A recoding of the quantum numbers and nothing more, chosen deliberately so that whatever it exhibits is a property of indexing rather than of atoms.

nodes.label: The Lach Cylinder — a hydrogenic cylinder over ν and over the transfer
nodes.rationale: The sign structure is bipartite, so no traverse reverses orientation an odd number of times — orientability is a structural reason, not an absence of evidence; ν grades every chain but never Λ itself, so the object is over ν, not graded by it.

nodes.label: Closed index — a fixed point of ℛ
nodes.rationale: Being a fixed point gives exactly six things — alphabet, bounds, totality of the membership test, admissible cells, adjoinable axes, imposable constraints — and never gives that the coordinates refer to anything.

nodes.label: ℛ — the closure operator over coordinate bounds
nodes.rationale: Extensive, monotone, idempotent; recovers value sets and pairwise monotone bounds from a set's own extension, and applies only to ordered coordinates.

nodes.label: E(X) = |ℛ(X)| − |X| — the closure defect
nodes.rationale: No novelty claimed for the machinery; the contribution is computing the closure defect of an index, where the periodic table's is 36 and Λ's is 0. Openness is a measurement and closure the case where it is zero.

nodes.label: The eight coordinates (n, ℓ, k, q, e, f, g, 2S)
Seven constraints, four origins
nodes.rationale: Exhaustiveness matters because it is the reason the object's properties can be attributed to indexing rather than to physics smuggled in through a bound; every constraint reads xᵢ ≤ φ(xⱼ), never a sum or difference.

nodes.label: The constraint graph is a tree (treewidth 1)
nodes.rationale: Eight nodes, seven edges, connected; an index whose constraint graph is a tree has its void in closed form and needs no sieve, because a tree has no cycles for inclusion–exclusion to correct.

nodes.label: F — the single generating expression for every cell
nodes.rationale: A closed expression exists because the coordinates couple only along a tree; F(1) = 976 and F(−1) = 2 at the caps of §7.4, and F(−1) = 2 has a cause rather than being a coincidence.

nodes.label: The void — the shadow of the exclusion principle
nodes.rationale: Void-free fraction 27.7–30.1% across 776 million pairs and a seventeenfold range in cell count; the excluded cells are exactly those Pauli, the hydrogenic bound or counting forbids.

nodes.label: d(x,y) — the occupancy measure on an interval
nodes.rationale: Between any two points there is an interval and the method returns its measure: the orders are partial and share 0.3%, but every pair of cells has a meet and a join, so the interval is total where the order is not.

nodes.label: Arithmetic encoding N(x) = ∏ pᵢ^{xᵢ}
nodes.rationale: Makes Λ a sublattice of the divisor lattice of a single integer, so that order becomes divisibility, join lcm, meet gcd, and rank Ω(N) — the two classical prime-counting functions arrive as the lattice's rank and its dimension bound, neither put there.

nodes.label: Seventeen join-irreducibles and twenty covering relations
nodes.rationale: All 976 down-sets of the 17-element poset are precisely the 976 cells — a fifty-seven-fold compression whose covers are the constraints made visible; the patterns hold at fifteen across six cap settings, which licenses stating the poset once.

nodes.label: Sperner, and not rank-symmetric
nodes.rationale: The rank sequence is log-concave hence unimodal, which is why Sperner holds rather than merely happening to; asymmetry denies a symmetric chain decomposition, so the classical divisor-lattice result does not transfer.

nodes.label: Rank conservation / rank modularity
nodes.rationale: A cheaper test than checking distributivity directly.

nodes.label: Order dimension of Λ
The caps convention (3,3,1,3,1)
nodes.rationale: Λ is infinite, so every count is stated at explicit caps; the counts change with the caps and the shape does not, and a cap-dependent figure without a stated cap is at these caps rather than unqualified.

nodes.label: The periodic table's defect — E = 36
nodes.rationale: The most successful index in the physical sciences is not closed, and the cost is exactly thirty-six cells: you have to be told period 1 holds two elements because the count of shells is not a coordinate of the table.

nodes.label: The calendar, repaired by relabelling
nodes.rationale: days(m) is not monotone in m, so nothing realises ℛ as printed (E = 7); relabelling months in order of length creates the monotone bound and E falls to 0 — a certificate checkable over 365 cells where brute force needs 12! relabellings.

nodes.label: The measured nuclide chart — E = 9 with no certificate
nodes.rationale: E unmoved at four proton cutoffs and pairing and clustering carry no axis, so the defect measures the world rather than the drawing; the drawn band closes because the drip lines are the envelopes.

nodes.label: Self-reference — alphabet, order, bounds
nodes.rationale: S1 and S3 hold generally; S2 — the order — is the hard one and works above d = 2 only by propagation along the tree, so Λ contains its own order.

nodes.label: Self-defence — a closed index contains its own contradiction
nodes.rationale: An index that holds only what its method consumes cannot catch a conclusion written against its own output; one that carries redundant quantities can, and did.

nodes.label: ⅅ = dim q − rank ∂Φ/∂p ≥ 1 — the counting argument
nodes.rationale: Requires no closure and no smoothness beyond differentiability; ⅅ counts functionally independent relations the derived quantities must satisfy, each a test the index must pass.

nodes.label: The ⅅ_phys / ⅅ_def split
nodes.rationale: Produced by refusing the conclusion that w = V·e detects nothing: a relation that cannot be violated by data is not empty, it is defending the derivation. Canonical under four unrelated perturbations.

nodes.label: Six disjoint defences, three of them not runnable by the book
nodes.rationale: The first four compare the book against the book; a conflation is an agreement between the book and itself about a word doing different work elsewhere, so no internal check can reach it.

nodes.label: χ_Λ total — totality catches a missing value
nodes.rationale: Only totality reaches the class where a guard returns a null and a caller coerces it to false; ⅅ ≥ 1 cannot, because the arithmetic downstream stays consistent.

nodes.label: ⅅ_ref — a term meaning one thing here and another in the theorem it was borrowed from
nodes.rationale: Establishing a referent requires reading someone else's theorem, so the verdict must be read and the mechanism is not runnable; paid once per coordinate. Worked case: the tower's 2K across jK, LK and jj.

nodes.label: ⅅ_dict — drift away from an established referent
nodes.rationale: Maintaining a referent is mechanical once a coordinate carries a stated one, so this runs forever after where ⅅ_ref is paid once.

nodes.label: ⅅ_gro — a term with no referent at all
nodes.rationale: q, the transfer coordinate, has no referent in the spectroscopic literature — not conflated, since there is nothing to conflate with, so ⅅ_ref cannot see it.

nodes.label: Extension — E1 cells, E2 axes, E3 constraints
nodes.rationale: Three operations and only three: change the cells, the axes, or the constraints. A cell may be added exactly when it sits in a hole whose joins and meets fall back into the lattice.

nodes.label: The law of realised closure
nodes.rationale: Restated in certificate form because the first form had no falsifier: 'realised' was never given a test, so the law was confirmed by naming and refutable only by failing to name, which §4.6 forbids.

nodes.label: The realiser — a certificate, exhibited and never found
nodes.rationale: A certificate is checkable where a search is not — 362 comparisons against eight and a half million — and brute force cannot reach Janet at all, since Janet is a different cell set drawn from the same 118 elements.

nodes.label: E(X) is the prediction budget
nodes.rationale: The number of predictions an index can make is E(X), and it is forced rather than observed; prediction lives only in the remainder, which for Λ is the quantum defect.

nodes.label: Completeness and predictiveness are alternatives
nodes.rationale: A prediction is a proposal about an unlisted cell and completeness is the property of having none — not a limitation discovered late but what completeness means.

nodes.label: Retrieval as a lattice problem
nodes.rationale: A paywall blocks a source, not a cell; the secondary can be better than the primary, and the retrieval graph is self-referencing, so an index should enumerate targets and navigate before searching.

nodes.label: ρ — retrieval depth, a property of (document, route)
nodes.rationale: The chapter collapsed the route index into a scalar; the route is a fibre, and §19.1 wrote it without using it — the fault Chapter 4 names as a coordinate collapsed into a count.

nodes.label: The tower — Λ₉ to Λ₁₃
nodes.rationale: Four axes added by battery return not five facts about five coordinates but one law met five times, and a shape that survives it.

nodes.label: Λ₉ composes — a category of transitions
nodes.rationale: Λ₈ cannot be iterated because its source carries four coordinates and its target three; 2S′ ≤ g supplies the missing spin and makes all targets legal sources, so composition is time — an order between cells rather than a stamp on one. The ninth axis was taken for seniority and arrived carrying this.

nodes.label: The dichotomy — counting axes exact, coupling axes envelopes
nodes.rationale: Three origins yield exact constraints; vector coupling yields an envelope (2S ≤ k at 48.5% density) that contains every physical multiplicity and admits values no k electrons can carry. Composability sorts the axes more strictly: an axis can be exact and not composable, none is composable and not exact.

nodes.label: The cylinder is a fibration with two-body fibres
nodes.rationale: The tree has two ends meeting at q, which is the shape of a two-body problem; as a bare product it fails (2,244 against 976) and conditioned on the coupling it separates exactly.

nodes.label: The electromagnetic index, inside Λ all along
nodes.rationale: Written as a congruence |Δℓ| ≡ γ (mod 2) the parity rule is an excluded form with E = 750; written as E1, M1, E2, M2 the same law is monotone and E = 0 — the notation was the coordinate that made the rule expressible.

nodes.label: A language is a coordinate system (P20)
nodes.rationale: The language a question is posed in bounds whether it can close, and at what cost — tree factorisation at 0.00018 s against Gröbner at 0.010 s; the documentary language has no closure mechanism at all, which is why precedent can be bounded and never settled.

nodes.label: Translation, and E as its price
nodes.rationale: One object under two namings carries two closure costs; E = 0 is relative to coordinates and the coordinates must be given, so a certificate is a translation exhibited and checked.

nodes.label: The cypher analysis — six languages asked of one object
nodes.rationale: It was not designed but noticed and then made explicit: a language that falls silent is the finding, and the identity of the silent language names the kind of object. Where analysis and statistics fall silent together the object is an integer object and fitting it is a category error.

nodes.label: Never fit across a language boundary
nodes.rationale: Every fit of the Löwdin session had been applied to the whole of the carried quantity a, and the constants kept absorbing one another because half the object was a finite set of surds with no analysis language. Enforced in code as the fourth question of the domain protocol.

nodes.label: The singleton criterion — a closed index has a singleton output class
nodes.rationale: ℛ cannot see it: δ and n* land in the same cell, so the closure operator finds no difference and only a separate criterion does. A quantity the work computes is not a quantity the index outputs.

nodes.label: SLACK — one quantity under three measures
nodes.rationale: All three forms are admitted against actual and differ only in being taken as a difference or a ratio; log of the occupancy measure is an ordinary ℓ¹ metric, which converts the additive form into the multiplicative one.

nodes.label: Slack is a description length
nodes.rationale: log SLACK = log|ℛ(X)| − log|X| is the information needed to say which subset X is, given its closure — the name was chosen before the quantity was analysed, and analysed it is a known object.

nodes.label: The bracket — T(n) lies between T(n−1) and T(n+1)
nodes.rationale: It fits nothing, assumes no functional form and returns an interval: a fit says where a level probably is, the bracket says where it cannot fail to be. Limit-free, and the price of limit-freedom is computed.

nodes.label: A bracket whose admissible set is a singleton
nodes.rationale: The same operation reads as a deduction about a quantity or as a uniqueness proof about a kind, and which it is depends only on how many admissible cells the interval contains.

nodes.label: The binder-mass window [119, 918] mₑ
nodes.rationale: Two monotone bounds with stated physical origins — fusion outrunning the cycle, and at least two molecular bound states — leave two known particles, and absorption removes the pion, so the muon is forced rather than selected.

nodes.label: V = w/e = 4ν/3 — the cost surface
nodes.rationale: V contains no σ, so no spectrometer can buy a narrower bracket — it is an impossibility statement, not an instrument, and a function of ν/h alone once h is carried through.

nodes.label: The algebraic floor V > 2 and the Rydberg floor 32/11
nodes.rationale: The floor owes nothing to atomic physics: the deductive interval always exceeds twice the error of the crudest point estimate built from the same two numbers, and the floor is approached only where two channels interleave — exactly where the method declines to operate.

nodes.label: The cost is the Newton decrement
nodes.rationale: The quantity has a name in another field, the term function is self-concordant, and that explains the cancellation — an attribution the book owes rather than a fresh discovery.

nodes.label: The pole at p = 1 — no guarantee for a linear observable
nodes.rationale: The pole sits on the field's favourite variable, which is why the cheapest-looking coordinate is the one that cannot be bracketed.

nodes.label: The Rydberg channel — fixed parent, fixed ℓ, varying n
δ — the quantum defect, the entire remainder
nodes.rationale: Λ is a property of the hydrogenic limit and δ is what is left, which is why perfecting the index moves nothing and why that is a theorem rather than a disappointment.

nodes.label: The collection — 153 channels across 35 atomic systems
nodes.rationale: Four numbers stand for one collection (1,442 / 1,105 / 869 / 930) and reconciling them needs twenty rows that are owed, so the chapter discloses rather than reconciles; the defect bracket passes 546 of 789 while the trivial bracket cannot fail.

nodes.label: Collective sections and the assembly rule
nodes.rationale: Every observable is a power of ν, so error amplifies as the exponent — which is the point rather than a flaw; collective coefficients are not a separate class.

nodes.label: The bound in the silence — a method that never failed has not been tested
nodes.rationale: Five exclusions are three mechanisms, and the collection never enters the failure regime — so the silence is a measurement: non-failure of a bracket yielded 1,061 perturbation bounds.

nodes.label: The register — 1,171 entries over three populations
nodes.rationale: The book cites an entry where the entry carries an argument and never reproduces the record, because a record reproduced in two places is a record with two versions; the register is the proof rather than the apology.

nodes.label: Withdrawals — the five that earned their place
nodes.rationale: The dominant pattern is prose asserting a conclusion while the contradicting output sits on the same screen; a book asserting verified cells and no failures is unfalsifiable without the list.

nodes.label: The wrong nuclear charge — the object catching its own author
nodes.rationale: Al II and K II computed at Z_eff = 1; the bracket held 56 of 56 and could not notice because Z cancels from containment, while two quantities the method never uses were loud immediately — the object found the error because it carried more than it needed.

nodes.label: The twenty-five prime audits, ordered by what a failure costs
nodes.rationale: Ten test the index, twelve test the book as an artefact and three test the register of objects; the split is stated rather than enforced because the artefact twelve have caught more faults than the index ten. An audit that reads the wrong artefact will pass anything.

nodes.label: Audit 7 — ATTRIBUTION
nodes.rationale: A missing attribution makes the book neither wrong nor unreadable nor unusable but dishonest, which is a worse failure and a quieter one; it exists because nine results were derived from scratch that were already in print.

nodes.label: The protocols — the failure modes of this work, inverted
nodes.rationale: Each prevents a specific failure and each failure occurred; they are not advice.

nodes.label: The principles P1–P23
nodes.rationale: Three were corrected by the act of formalising them; sorted by what a principle is rather than by whether an expression exists, they fall into mechanism, operation and relation, and P16 has no register entry because it was adopted rather than learned.

nodes.label: The grid — read the empty cells rather than hunting for them
nodes.rationale: Chapter 6 applied to the book's own ignorance: the first empty cell in a column is the whole obstacle and everything below it is downstream — twenty-two formulations were attempts on four cells that depend on one.

nodes.label: Triangulation — three results locate a fourth
nodes.rationale: Three measurements of one thing are not three facts; they are a position, and it is a check as well as a method.

nodes.label: §2.14 — compute, then write
nodes.rationale: Exists because the failure was measured rather than deplored: writing conclusions before reading output happens as readily on six cells as on 1,442, so it is not a failure of attention and no amount of care fixes it.

nodes.label: §2.13 — commit before you look
nodes.rationale: Prevents a choice that depended on its own answer — the anchoring failure — and is what protects against an index being replaced rather than contradicted.

nodes.label: §2.8 — two independent routes
nodes.rationale: Prevents an undetectable derivation error (w = 3ν·e); 'never one heuristic' is the same rule stated for instruments, and §2.24 names the one thing §2.8 does not say.

nodes.label: §2.20 — the prime directive: nothing runs unbounded
Redundancy of paths, not redundancy of care
nodes.rationale: Four different things were looking and they were not looking at the same thing — the object, the protocols, the audits and the collaborator each catch a class the others cannot. The book's central claim, tested on its own production.

nodes.label: Ten failure mechanisms, each earned by a failure that happened
nodes.rationale: Not a taxonomy assembled in advance; every mechanism was extracted from the register after the fact, and §28.7.9 adds the level a fault landed at — value, derivation or inference — which merges two the list keeps apart.

nodes.label: The reorderability law
nodes.rationale: Arity is the number of axes on which two cells differ: at arity ≤ 3 the language is bijunctive and the problem linear, at arity ≥ 4 it contains 1-in-3-SAT and no Schaefer class covers it. The procedure and the hardness are one statement read at two regimes.

nodes.label: The step law
nodes.rationale: Growth from the minimal reorderable sets reaches every reorderable set, with step size measured exhaustively across twelve boxes; the objects it counts had been catalogued decades earlier.

nodes.label: The strict-nesting lemma for monotone interval endpoints
nodes.rationale: Discharged without a linear-time algorithm; 'strictly' is load-bearing, since reading it as ordinary containment refutes the lemma on 1,098 of 2,354 interval sets — the reading tried first and wrong, which is why the qualifier is in the statement.

nodes.label: Order recovery above the tree
nodes.rationale: Exists because a conclusion that Λ did not contain its own order was refused and the reasoning resumed from the refusal.

nodes.label: The method outside spectroscopy
nodes.rationale: A method that transfers is a different claim from one that fits, so it is run on four subjects it was not built for; sensitive dependence destroys monotonicity along a chaotic trajectory, so what transfers is families rather than trajectories.

nodes.label: The Calabi–Yau catalogue as an index
nodes.rationale: The thin tip is removable not by re-coordinatising but by re-constructing, so it is a defect of the index like the periodic table's 36; and the Pareto share must be read against the right denominator — 0.221%, not 0.0002%.

nodes.label: Three string-theory objects on the pole
nodes.rationale: Second difference zero means two levels determine every other exactly, so a bracket is unnecessary; the content sits in the degeneracy, and the partition function is Λ's expression with counts where F has booleans.

nodes.label: Celestial mechanics — families, not trajectories
The nucleus — a second index of the same construction
The Löwdin challenge
nodes.rationale: The target is the order, not n+ℓ: deriving n+ℓ exactly would mean deriving something false at two elements, since Madelung inverts 5d/4f and 6d/5f.

nodes.label: ν(n,ℓ,q) = n − a·√(n − ℓ − 1 + q/2(2ℓ+1)) — the occupation law
nodes.rationale: Both Pauli quantities appear — the capacity governs admissibility and sits inside the radicand — and occupancy enters only through Pauli, so the law needs no new coordinate; no parameter is fitted and it is exceptionless on 106 elements including every aufbau anomaly.

nodes.label: The n+ℓ (Madelung) rule
nodes.rationale: A name for the order that is 89% accurate: seventeen of nineteen openings agree, two do not.

nodes.label: The walk — `a` carried between elements, resetting eighteen times
nodes.rationale: Every reset is a subshell opening, an aufbau exception or the return from one, and it never resets mid-subshell, which is why each subshell fills at constant a. The state is necessary: without a carried value 104 of 106 steps admit several self-consistent subshells, so the periodic table is not computable from a single atom's configuration.

nodes.label: The corridor L(Z) < a < U(Z)
nodes.rationale: One linear inequality per rival, intersecting in an interval; all 106 non-empty over nineteen distinct surds, with no measurement entering — only Pauli's capacity and the node count.

nodes.label: Λ_var — the index of the problem's variables
nodes.rationale: Placing every variable on (body, role) closes at E = 0 and leaves the nucleus–rydberg row empty.

nodes.label: Screening as a fact about the coordinates
nodes.rationale: A claim about the index, not the interaction: the nucleus does attract the outer electron strongly, but no coordinate carries that attraction unmediated — which is why the channel equation is a core–rydberg factor times a nucleus–core factor with no third factor.

nodes.label: The three electronic ladders and the untraced isotopic fourth
nodes.rationale: Because Z = Nₑ + c − 1 only two of three electronic quantities are independent, so no ladder varies Z alone; the isotopic ladder is orthogonal to all three, is the only route to the nucleus, and has never been traced.

nodes.label: The entry point t(ℓ) → √(ℓ(ℓ+1)/2)
nodes.rationale: ℓ(ℓ+1) is the centrifugal term, the only place ℓ enters the radial Schrödinger equation; measured as a limit approached along n rather than a constant, with 6p sitting 0.2% above the centrifugal value.

nodes.label: The law applied to this book
nodes.rationale: The book is an index, so its own closure, self-reference and self-defence are computable and its recursion has a stated stopping point; the recursion is safe because the logic carries no negation.

nodes.label: Appendix A — Proofs
nodes.rationale: Seventeen statements, ten proved in place in the chapters and seven written out here; projections of closed sets are closed but the converse fails, because closure is a d-dimensional condition.

nodes.label: Appendix B — Data and provenance
nodes.rationale: Every number traces to a named compilation, table and page, or to a computation whose code is stated.

nodes.label: Appendix D — The book's mathematics, indexed
nodes.rationale: The first attempt failed because ℛ recovers monotone bounds and applies to ordered coordinates only; the repair is Λ's own shape — fibre over the categorical axes and put the ordered coordinates inside. Closing it forced two constraints the book had never stated.

nodes.label: Appendix E — Q, the book's ignorance indexed
nodes.rationale: Q was recomputed five times and each recomputation was written beside its predecessor, so three live item counts stood at once; an index states its current contents once and its history as history.

nodes.label: Appendix F — The book's printed numbers, indexed
nodes.rationale: What is not indexed cannot be closed, and what is not closed carries defects no audit is shaped to find; 70% of occurrences stand in a paragraph with no method, code or section cue — a count of numbers the book cannot sort into recheckable and not.

nodes.label: Löwdin (1969) — the n+ℓ challenge
nodes.author: Per-Olov Löwdin

nodes.label: Bergman's double-projection theorem
nodes.rationale: A sublattice of a finite product of lattices is determined by its two-fold projections, so E(Λ) = 0 is the discovery that Λ is a sublattice, and the proof in §16.1 is correct and fifty years late.

nodes.label: Baker and Pixley (1975)
Montanari (1974), Networks of constraints
nodes.author: U. Montanari

nodes.label: Dechter (1992), From local to global consistency
nodes.author: R. Dechter

nodes.label: Freuder (1982) — cited for backtrack-free search, not global consistency
nodes.author: E. C. Freuder
nodes.rationale: The book had been citing Freuder for Dechter's theorem; the mis-citation is corrected at register 400.

nodes.label: Deville, Barták and Van Hentenryck (1999) — staircase constraints
nodes.rationale: φ̂ recovers exactly a staircase constraint, so the operator of §6.1 has been building a named object since Chapter 6.

nodes.label: van Beek and Dechter (1995, 1997) — row convexity and constraint tightness
nodes.rationale: The tight-pair count is exactly twice the book's envelope-step number S, and it is that count rather than the tightness level the seed cost tracks; the tightness half of the entry went unused for four cycles.

nodes.label: Dilworth (1950) — decomposition theorem
nodes.author: R. P. Dilworth

nodes.label: Birkhoff's representation theorem
Rival (1973/74) — lattice embedding and irreducible intervals
nodes.author: I. Rival

nodes.label: Larson (1998)
Siggers (2016) — Lemma 3.5(ii) states φ_ij exactly
Booth and Lueker — linear PQ-tree construction
Tucker (1972) — the obstruction family
Edlén (1964), examined at one remove

nodes.rationale: Every equation in the review is a fit and the paradigm is stated twice explicitly, so the near miss is not this book's result; a bibliographic correction follows.

nodes.label: NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12)
nodes.rationale: Cited for the three-way provenance marking of level values — plain, [ ] and ( ) — which is what §24.9's per-species caveat rests on.

nodes.label: The Kreuzer–Skarke list of reflexive 4-polytopes
Batyrev's polar duality
Candelas, de la Ossa, He and Szendrői — Triadophilia (ATMP 12, 2008)
nodes.rationale: A slice specified exactly in print is enough for the operator even when the full catalogue file cannot be read.

nodes.author: Matthew Lach

nodes.label: Cowan and Andrew (1965) — the four pure coupling schemes
nodes.rationale: Cited for the grouping of LS, LK, jK and jj as a single set, not only for its members — a precedent for the set the tower rebuilds.
